The College of Nursing offers 3 nurse practitioner (NP) specialty tracks within its MS program and its Post-MS Certificate Program. These include Adult-Gerontology Primary Care NP, Family NP and Psychiatric-Mental Health NP (PMHNP). The first two of these specialties focus on primary care and are identical in terms of total credits in the MS Program (42) and very similar in terms of coursework and other program requirements. The PMHNP specialty track is the newest specialty track offered within the MS program

2 and currently requires 48 - 49 credits.
Having just graduated their first few graduates in the PMHNP specialty track, the PMHNP program faculty, the MS/DNP Program Committee and Associate Dean Kathy Hutchinson all agreed that revisions were needed within the PMHNP specialty track to address 3 issues.
The 3 issues and proposed changes to the PMHNP specialty track are outlined below and shown in Appendix A: (1) the credit allocations for some of the courses within the PMHNP specialty (e.g., NUR 545) needed to be corrected to be more consistent with university standards and other course offerings within the program.
NUR 545 focuses on psychiatric-mental health care for children, adolescents and families and is a 2 credit course.
In contrast, NUR 513 focuses on psychiatric-mental health care for adults and is a 3 credit course.

The didactic NP specialty courses in the other NP specialty tracks are all 3 credit courses. (2) In addition to correcting the inconsistency in credit allocations to didactic courses, the faculty and MS/DNP cmte. sought to address uneven distribution of clinical practicum credits across the PMHNP clinical courses (NUR 514, 546 and 547) and align these credits with those in the other NP specialty tracks.
The current PMHNP specialty requires 500- 600+ clinical hours and the 3 clinical courses total 15 credits.
In comparison, the other specialty tracks require similar clinical hours but allocate only 12 credits across their 3 clinical courses. (3) In order to be consistent with recommendations from our accrediting body (The American Association of Colleges of Nursing / CCNE), the CON implemented a single course addressing Advanced Health Assessment / Physical Assessment Across the Lifespan (NUR 530) In Fall, 2021.
This 4 credit didactic and lab course will now be completed by students in all 3 nurse practitioner specialty tracks in the MS program.
In the past, PMHNP students took an abbreviated 3 credit course in health assessment (NUR 501).

This change alone would result in an additional 1 credit increase to the PMHNP track of the MS curriculum.
The number of credits for this specialty track is already high.
Addressing the issues in (1) and (3) above would result in a 1 - 2 credit increase in the number of credits in the PMHNP specialty track.
Balancing this against the need to reduce clinical credits in (2) above, would result in an overall reduction in the number of credits for the PMHNP specialty track in the MS program from 48-49 to 47.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) Background: This proposal is requesting the addition of tracks to an existing degree program, the MS in Dietetics. This is being requested because the program is seeking accreditation by its external credentialing agency. We are requesting that the MS degree now has two tracks – one for students completing the accredited program and one for students who are not completing the accredited program. Currently, the degree does not have any tracks. The MS in Dietetics Program has been in existence since 2015. It was created in partnership with Sodexo Dietetic Internship in anticipation of the 2024 entry level 11/28/2021 12/14/2021

2 credentialing requirement which states that all students need a master’s degree with experiential learning to become Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs).
Until 2024, a BS degree and an internship that provides experiential learning are required to become a RDN.
This change prompted free-standing internships to partner with universities to meet this new degree requirement.
The University of Rhode Island has successfully worked with Sodexo to provide a master’s degree to its interns for the past 6 years.
We are now formalizing the existing partnership with Sodexo by becoming an accredited Future Graduate Program to meet the Future Education Model (FEM) Standards as outlined by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).
The FEM requires enhanced integration between the didactic and experiential components as part of the accreditation.
Curriculum changes to meet the new standards were approved in the spring of 2021.
The FEM Program will begin in the fall of 2022.
Students who complete these requirements need to be in a separate track to best manage our accreditation.
In 2018, URI expanded the master’s degree offering to RDNs employed by Sodexo.

This program was requested by Sodexo to help their current RDNs to remain competitive with new graduates entering the workforce with master’s degrees.
RDNs complete the MS degree in a separate cohort, and complete individualized learning experiences instead of the standard experiential learning rotations.
We are requesting a second non-accredited track in the MS in Dietetics degree to allow us to continue to offer the program to these students and to students who are unable to complete the accredited track.
The MS in Dietetics has graduated 217 students as of December 2021.

Two tracks are being requested to allow one track to become an accredited program and for the second track to serve students, predominately Sodexo RDNs, not seeking the accredited program.

The RDNs cannot participate in the new FEM program since it will be an accredited program that includes integrated didactic and experiential learning and they have already completed the experiential component.

Sodexo has a new initiative to advance RDN’s education to the graduate level and offers tuition reimbursement to incentivize RDNs to obtain graduate degrees.

To date, we have accommodated Sodexo’s needs to train their RDNs in our online master’s program but they will not be eligible for the FEM track.
